p: Cardiff Bay is perfect for a stroll after a morning of science. The Pierhead Building, a striking red-brick Victorian landmark, is free to visit and tells the story of the bay's history. Nearby, the Norwegian Church Arts Centre is a pretty white wooden church where Roald Dahl was baptised. It's now a café and arts space.

For a longer walk, the Cardiff Bay Barrage links the bay to Penarth. It's a flat, traffic-free route with views across the water and a play area along the way. Penarth has a Victorian pier and a lovely seafront for an ice cream.
If you fancy a boat trip, water taxis and tour boats run around the bay and up the River Taff towards the city centre.

Tips for Techniquest: weekends and school holidays can be busy, so arrive early for the calmest experience. Set some time aside for the science theatre and planetarium, as these shows are often the highlight. Bring snacks and water, and allow a good few hours so nobody has to rush.

Hungry? Mermaid Quay is right on the doorstep, with restaurants and cafés overlooking the water, so you can watch the boats come and go while the kids chatter about everything they've just tried. On a sunny day, the Bay feels almost Mediterranean. Almost. Bring a brolly, just in case, because this is still Wales.
